notes:
Airline-AGNOSTIC fallback rule (ADR-026): looked up by id, never by IATA (empty iataCodes), and run only when no airline rule exists or the airline rule's parse failed. Anchors come from the 2026-09-22 recon (docs/recon/google-flights-NOTES.md + captured panel HTML): the visible

Flight status

heading is the presence sentinel (absent entirely when Google shows no rich card — clean failure), ARIA roles/attributes and the closed English label vocabulary (hl=en pins it) are the anchors; Google's short obfuscated CSS classes (ngrL4, cZmqkf, ZuFvNc, ...) rotate per deploy and are deliberately NEVER used. The data-maindata JSON blob on div[data-bkt=onebox] is Google's own app data (flight_status enums, signed delay minutes) — captured as diagnostics; it lists leg INSTANCES across the date window in an order that does not align with the date tabs for multi-leg flights (AI101: 6 entries vs 4 tabs), so status is derived from the rendered card instead. Per-card detail extraction (header status, dep/arr label+time, original time, Terminal/Gate, city·date) needs tab→panel ARIA references and sibling pairing the declarative schema cannot express — it lives in feature:flights' pure GoogleFlightsExtractor, run on the same dump (ScrapeEvent.Extracted.rawHtml). readySignal fires once results (or a bot-wall captcha form) rendered: the anonymous first response is a JS challenge shell (no #rso/#search) that redirects itself, so waiting for the results container is what makes the dump land on the real page. dismissSelectors are DEFENSIVE (no consent wall was seen from an India egress; EU users are known to be redirected to consent.google.com). v2 (2026-09-22 live validation): the query carries the journey DATE ({date}, expanded by the feature as `22+September+2026`) because a bare `SG 128 flight status` pre-selected the NEXT operating day (Wed 23 Sept, a Scheduled card) while the journey's day (Tue 22 Sept) was CANCELLED - with the date in the query Google selects that day's tab and renders its card (verified for SG 128, 6E 541, 6E 6353, 6E 6144, 6E 9468). The live DOM also renders the same card TWICE inside the data-dates container (a second copy sits in a hidden role=dialog carrying its own role=tablist), and multi-leg flights render several cards for ONE date (6E 9468 AUH-BLR + BLR-IXE) - both handled by the feature parser (dialog copies skipped, card chosen by the journey's date, then airports, then scheduled time).
